summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Mumbai and a doctorate from Heidelberg University. He served as Hon. Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001) and held professorships at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ramesh Chandra Negi works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as a research assistant (attested 2001–2004) and associate professor (attested 2026), and taught Ruth Gamble and Andy Rotman.

Historian and Indologist Ramesh Chandra Majumdar earned degrees from Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as professor and provost at the University of Dhaka, president of the Asiatic Society (1966–1968), and held teaching posts at Chicago and Pennsylvania.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. In 1967, he was head of the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Calcutta. He was affiliated with Ananda Mohan College (attested 1999–2003).
Ramon Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).

Ran Mao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who earned degrees from Hainan University and a PhD from Kasetsart University (2020). He taught Chinese at institutions including Hainan University, KU Leuven, and Guizhou University of Finance and Economics (2020–2022).
Randall Studstill is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Richard Payne and teacher Steven D. Goodman.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He held professorships at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2006) and Beijing Normal University (2021–2023).

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha. He is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught numerous prominent students, including Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.
Raniero Gnoli was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranjeet Kumar Verma is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Lucknow and held a scholar post at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad in 2025.
Rano Hodžiakbarovna Guljamova was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from around 1957 to 1962 and subsequently taught there from 1962 to 1985.
Ranu Kunwar pursued PhD studies at the Australian National University between 2022 and 2026 under the supervision of Assa Doron.

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held posts as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017) and was affiliated with Santa Clara University (attested 2012).

Raoul Curiel worked in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Émile Benveniste. He served in the DAFA, as Director-General of Pakistan's archaeology department, and at the Cabinet des Médailles (1965–1978).
Raphael Kühner was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (circa 1820–1824). He taught Georg Bühler.
Raphael Marozzi was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Washington (~1946–1949) and an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1949–1952).
